dimensions.name: Requirements and scope
dimensions.description: Clarifies the feed product, consistency expectations, ranking goals, and what is out of scope.

levels.1: Repeats the prompt without defining the feed or consistency expectations.
levels.2: Lists features but ignores ranking, pagination, or eventual consistency.
levels.3: Separates functional and non-functional requirements and states freshness and latency assumptions.
levels.4: Also distinguishes Following vs For You behavior, quantifies acceptable staleness, and names the ranking objective.

dimensions.name: API and pagination
dimensions.description: Defines feed, post, follow, and counter interfaces with stable pagination.

levels.1: No clear feed or post API.
levels.2: Defines a feed endpoint but uses offset pagination or omits errors.
levels.3: Defines cursor pagination, post creation, follow/unfollow, and error cases.
levels.4: Also covers idempotent post creation, new-posts indicators, blocking, and how clients merge paginated pages.

dimensions.name: Post and feed storage
dimensions.description: Chooses post, follow, and feed-entry schemas, keys, and storage engines.

levels.1: No concrete schema or storage choice.
levels.2: Has a posts table but no feed or follow model.
levels.3: Defines posts, follows, and precomputed feed entries with keys and a storage engine.
levels.4: Also discusses sharding, retention, media references, counter storage, and how deletes propagate.

dimensions.name: Fan-out architecture
dimensions.description: Separates post creation, fan-out, feed reads, ranking, and counters.

levels.1: Generates the feed by scanning all follows on every read.
levels.2: Names a fan-out worker but does not show the write or read path.
levels.3: Shows post creation, asynchronous fan-out, feed storage, read path, and ranking.
levels.4: Also explains the hybrid push/pull split for celebrities, cache layers, and how degraded ranking falls back.

dimensions.name: Scale and performance
dimensions.description: Sizes feed reads, fan-out amplification, cache hit rate, and storage.

levels.1: Ignores the read volume or fan-out cost.
levels.2: Repeats the numbers without estimating QPS, cache size, or storage amplification.
levels.3: Estimates feed QPS, fan-out write amplification, cache size, and storage.
levels.4: Also quantifies tail latency, hot-account behavior, ranking cost per candidate, and the cost of retention.

dimensions.name: Trade-offs
dimensions.description: Compares push vs pull, precomputed vs on-demand ranking, and consistency choices.

levels.2: Names fan-out on write or read without connecting it to the design.
levels.3: Compares at least two meaningful choices, such as push vs pull or precomputed vs ranked-at-read.
levels.4: Also explains when the chosen model is wrong, how freshness is traded for latency, and what would trigger a redesign.

dimensions.name: Failure modes and operations
dimensions.description: Covers fan-out backlog, hot accounts, cache failures, stale feeds, and monitoring.

levels.1: Assumes fan-out and caches never fail.
levels.2: Mentions retries or a queue without a recovery path.
levels.3: Identifies the main failure modes and the metrics or alerts that detect them.
levels.4: Also covers degraded feed modes, celebrity posts, cache stampedes, delete propagation, and runbook-level recovery.
